title: Machine learning for predicting high axillary nodal burden in breast cancer patients with positive sentinel lymph nodes.
summary: Models using clinical and pathology features predicted high axillary nodal burden in sentinel-node-positive breast cancer; the retrospective cohort was split into training and validation sets, so prospective clinical utility remains unproven. The result is reported in the World Journal of Surgical Oncology. It does not establish generalization beyond the reported setting or prospective real-world benefit.
ai_technology: Nine machine-learning models were trained on clinicopathological features to predict high axillary nodal burden; LASSO and Boruta selected features, and SHAP interpreted the model.
